title: BioHarvest Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results and Provides Business Update
summary: Prioritizes cash preservation and controlled VINIA growth while concentrating CDMO resources on advanced programs with near-term manufacturing potential Vancouver, British Columbia and Rehovot, Israel - November 12, 2026 - BioHarvest Sciences Inc (Nasdaq: BHST) (TASE: BHST) (FSE: 8MV0), a leader in Botanical Synthesis technology and sustainable plant-based molecule development, today reported financial results for the three and nine months
body_markdown:
- *Prioritizes cash preservation and controlled VINIA growth while concentrating CDMO resources on advanced programs with near-term manufacturing potential*


**Vancouver, British Columbia and Rehovot, Israel – November 12, 2026** -[BioHarvest Sciences Inc](https://api.newsfilecorp.com/redirect/4YV7LuWP1J) (Nasdaq: BHST) (TASE: BHST) (FSE: 8MV0), a leader in Botanical Synthesis technology and sustainable plant-based molecule development, today reported financial results for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, and outlined its strategic priorities for 2027. The Company is aligning capital allocation, operating expenses and development resources with a narrower set of commercial objectives designed to preserve liquidity and advance its most promising Botanical Synthesis programs toward manufacturing.


*All figures stated in this news release are in U.S. dollars unless stated otherwise.*


**Third Quarter and 2026 Financial Results Highlights**


- Q3 2026 revenue was $7.9 million, compared with $8.8 million in Q2 2026 and $9.1 million in Q3 2025. The decline reflected the Company’s deliberate moderation of lower-return customer acquisition in the Products Business Unit, as part of its strategy to build a healthier, more profitable revenue base, as well as the timing of CDMO development revenue. Gross margin was 54%, compared with 58% in Q2 2026 and approximately 61% in Q3 2025, reflecting a revenue mix weighted toward Products, with a lower contribution from higher-margin CDMO development revenue.
- Operating loss was $3 million, compared with $2.5 million in Q2 2026 and $0.9 million in Q3 2025. The sequential increase reflected lower gross profit, partly offset by lower operating expenses quarter over quarter, while the year-over-year increase reflected higher gross profit in Q3 2025, as well as one-time, non-cash revaluation income recognized in that quarter, both of which resulted in a lower operating loss in Q3 2025 compared with Q3 2026.
- Cash, cash equivalents and bank deposits totaled $12.5 million at September 30, 2026, versus $16.2 million at June 30, 2026 and $23 million at December 31, 2025.


“Our third-quarter results reflect a period of deliberate transition,” Commented Dr. Zaki Rakib, CEO and Executive Chairman, adding, ”Consistent with a cash-disciplined strategy, we are making a fundamental choice about how BioHarvest creates value: protecting our cash, growing VINIA with better economics, and concentrating our CDMO capabilities on fewer programs that can reach manufacturing sooner.


“Toward the end of the second quarter, we began implementing changes to VINIA’s marketing and sales strategy designed to drive profitability. These changes have resulted in a moderate decline in revenue, which we anticipated as part of our sales and marketing efficiency initiatives, and we expect the benefits of these improvements along with revenue growth to become evident beginning in the first quarter of 2027. On the CDMO development side, we are focusing our resources on the fragrance compound, multiple sweetener compounds with Tate & Lyle, and the Saffron development projects. Our new business development activity is focused on licensing our unique molecules’ assets.


“We believe focus—not the number of projects in development—will determine our speed of commercialization and ultimately our returns on invested capital.”


##
**Three execution priorities**


- **Cash preservation and conditional manufacturing investment** .


- The Company intends to add manufacturing capacity gradually, in phases aligned with demonstrated demand, in order to preserve cash.


- Reduction of fixed operation costs, including consolidation of development sites in 2027.


- **Controlled VINIA growth** . Management intends to prioritize efficient customer acquisition, retention, margin discipline and cash contribution rather than pursuing top-line growth irrespective of economics.


- **CDMO focus on select programs and faster progression.** Resources will be concentrated on programs with the clearest commercial and manufacturing pathways.


2027 priorities include; completing development of three advanced projects – the rare, high-value, plant-based fragrance ingredient, the Saffron compound, and the natural sweetener molecules; and licensing our unique molecules’ assets. The aim is to move advanced assets into production and commercialization with greater speed and lower resource dispersion.


**Third Quarter and Recent Operational Highlights**


- In August, the Company signed the CDMO division’s first manufacturing and supply agreement, an exclusive agreement covering the scaled production of a rare, high-value, plant-based fragrance ingredient. The agreement extends an existing multi-stage development program with a UAE-based customer.


The source plant is endangered due to overharvesting and habitat loss, and the ingredient is widely regarded as one of the most valuable fragrance raw materials in the world, with premium grades commanding prices exceeding tens of thousands of U.S. dollars per kilogram.


Following the successful completion of Stage 1 development in March 2026, Stage 2 was initiated in May and is expected to be completed within six to nine months. The manufacturing and supply agreement provides for the production of an anticipated 20 tons of the fragrance composition, and BioHarvest anticipates that limited production of this ingredient could begin as early as the first quarter of 2027.


- In September, BioHarvest launched single-dose VINIA Daily Chews, designed to complement the existing VINIA portfolio, broaden consumer choice and provide an additional pathway for customer acquisition, retention, market expansion and revenue growth.


VINIA also demonstrates the commercial versatility of the Botanical Synthesis platform. Botanical Synthesis produces plant-based compositions in a versatile powder format, and VINIA gives prospective CDMO customers a commercial example of how a BioHarvest composition can progress from plant-cell development through scaled manufacturing and into differentiated consumer formats.


**Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results Summary**


Revenues for the third quarter of 2026 were $7.9 million, compared to $9.1 million in the same year-ago quarter. The decrease reflects a planned shift to profitable growth in the Products Business Unit and the timing of CDMO development revenue.


Cost of revenue was $3.6 million, compared to $3.5 million for the same period last year.


Gross profit in the third quarter of 2026 was $4.2 million, or 54% of total revenue, as compared to $5.6 million, or 61% of total revenue, in the same year-ago quarter. The change reflects the mix of revenues in the quarter, which was weighted toward Products Business Unit revenue, with a lower contribution from higher-margin CDMO development revenue.


R&D expenses totaled $1.8 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $1.4 million for the same period last year. The increase was primarily driven by higher technology development expenditures within the CDMO Services Business Unit, due to the need to accelerate the development for the rare fragrance composition in light of the supply agreement that was signed.


Sales and marketing expenses totaled $4.0 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $4.1 million for the same period last year.


G&A expenses totaled $1.5 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $0.9 million for the same period last year. The increase primarily reflects one-time income of $0.4 million recognized in the third quarter of 2025, which offset expenses in the comparative period.


Net loss for the third quarter of 2026 totaled $3.3 million, or $0.15 per basic and diluted share, compared to a net loss of $2.5 million, or $0.14 per basic and diluted share, for the same period last year.


Adjusted EBITDA loss – a non-IFRS measure – totaled $2.0 million, compared to $0.4 million in the same year-ago quarter. Under the two-lens approach, the third quarter Adjusted EBITDA losses of the CDMO services and Products divisions are $1.4 million and $0.6 million respectively, as compared $0.2 million and $0.2 million in the same year ago quarter.


Cash and cash equivalents, together with bank deposits, as of September 30, 2026 totaled $12.5 million, compared to $11 million as of September 30, 2025.


***Full-Year 2026 Guidance*** **


In order to set the Company for success in 2027 and creating substantial shareholder value, the actions taken in the beginning of Q3 have resulted in changes to the 2026 financial results.


Full-year revenue guidance for the VINIA D2C business has been revised to $31–$32 million, while Adjusted EBITDA loss guidance remains unchanged at $1.5-$2.5 million.


Largely driven by the 20-ton plant-based fragrance supply agreement (estimated to generate revenue of $20- $30 million in 2027-2028) now requiring faster development and an enhanced allocation of resources, fewer new projects than expected will be initiated in 2026. As a result, the CDMO business has revised its expected full-year revenue range to $1–$1.5 million and now anticipates a full-year Adjusted EBITDA loss of $4–$5 million.


On a consolidated basis, the Company now expects full-year 2026 revenue of $32–$33.5 million and an Adjusted EBITDA loss in the range of $5.5–$7.5 million.

**Use of Non-IFRS Financial Measures**


This press release includes Adjusted EBITDA, a non-IFRS measure, including on a segment basis for the CDMO Services and Products business units. Adjusted EBITDA is not a standardized financial measure under IFRS and might not be comparable to similar financial measures disclosed by other issuers. It should not be considered as an alternative to operating loss or any other measure of financial performance under IFRS. Adjusted EBITDA represents operating profit (loss) before depreciation and amortization, adjusted for share-based payment. The Company believes this non-IFRS measure, when considered together with the corresponding IFRS measures, provides useful information to investors and management regarding financial and business trends relating to the Company’s results of operations. However, this non-IFRS measure has significant limitations in that it does not reflect all the costs and other items associated with the operation of the Company’s business as determined in accordance with IFRS. Investors should consider non-IFRS measures in addition to, and not as a substitute for, or superior to, measures of financial performance in accordance with IFRS. **About BioHarvest**


BioHarvest (NASDAQ: BHST) (TASE: BHST) (FSE: 8MV0) is a leader in Botanical Synthesis, leveraging its patented technology platform to grow plant-based compounds, without the need to grow the underlying plant. BioHarvest is leveraging its botanical synthesis technology to develop the next generation of science-based and clinically proven therapeutic solutions within two major business verticals: as a contract development and manufacturing organization (CDMO) on behalf of customers seeking novel plant-based compounds, and as a creator of proprietary nutraceutical health and wellness products based on its botanical synthesis technology. To learn more, please visit[www.bioharvest.com](https://api.newsfilecorp.com/redirect/JkD71FAOg4) .
